notes: Under A141 a credential needs its credits, not only paid elapsed periods. Each period a student attempts the program's on-time share of credits, and the share they earn slides with the weekly hours they owe elsewhere (work, care and other commitments from the life-load record): 1 / (1 + max(0, hours - 15) / 30). The two sizes are PLACEHOLDER in STUDY_CREDIT_PACE, src/simulation/education-study-progression.ts.

Credit requirements use common totals: 30 for a one-year certificate, 60 for an associate degree, 120 for a bachelor's degree, 36 for a master's degree, and 83 for a J.D. (the ABA's minimum, Standard 311(a)). Saved terms without a requirement read thirty credits an academic year.

A student short of credits keeps studying and paying one period at a time up to 150% of the planned length, the federal maximum timeframe for satisfactory academic progress (34 CFR 668.34(b)), applied here to every student, not only those receiving federal aid.
question: How does the number of hours a college student works or spends caregiving each week change the share of attempted credits they complete in a term, and what credit totals do certificate, associate, bachelor's and master's programs require across U.S. colleges?

sourcesChecked.source: NCES, The Condition of Education, College Student Employment indicator

Sets the 150% maximum timeframe and a pace measure for aid eligibility; it does not say how outside hours affect earned credits.

title: How outside hours change the credits a student earns
usableAnswer: Credit-completion rates (credits earned over credits attempted) by weekly hours worked or caregiving, from a national survey such as NPSAS or BPS, so the curve in STUDY_CREDIT_PACE can be measured; and typical credit totals by credential level.
whyItMatters: Without credits, paying for the years was enough to graduate, so a student working full time finished a degree as surely as one who studied full time, and the player's choices about work and study did not matter.

answer.summary: Federal guidance gives approximate1instruction+2outside work hours per semester credit per week, with alternative equivalents. It does not estimate credits completed versus paid work/caregiving, or impose uniform credential totals.
answer.stillOpen: No net-price/aid-share distribution, causal credits-work response, comprehensive admissions/calendar rules, actual school closure hazard or all56 regional cost model.
